extracted.intended_audience: policy designers, agency officials, civic-technology researchers, and organizers working on public participation in administrative rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for producing and designing public comments and civic-engagement systems for administrative notice-and-comment rulemaking that increase the value of participation to agencies. Emphasizes quality criteria for comments and design principles for outreach and platform design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage with the specific provisions of the rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments that engage with the specific provisions of the rule
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target comments to particular sections, language, or provisions rather than making only general assertions; show how proposed or existing text would affect regulated behavior or obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide information on real-world impacts agencies cannot easily access
rubrics_metrics.description: Information on real-world impacts the agency cannot easily access
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contribute situated, experiential facts about how rules operate on the ground (e.g., practical constraints, implementation barriers, contextual details) rather than abstract preferences or easily-hired technical expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer substantive responses to the agency's stated questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Substantive responses to the agency's stated questions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directly address questions posed in the notice (NPRM) with evidence, concrete examples, data where available, and reasoned argument that helps the agency choose among alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use accessible, non-technical language while remaining substantively grounded
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of accessible, non-technical language while remaining substantively grounded
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write so that non-experts and agency staff can understand the point, avoiding unnecessary jargon but maintaining substantive content and supporting evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize 'knowledge in the people' (situated, experiential knowledge)
rubrics_metrics.description: The most valuable contribution citizens make is 'knowledge in the people' — situated, experiential knowledge that agencies cannot otherwise access
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize lived experience and concrete observations about how rules affect people and operations; distinguish such contributions from technical/legal expertise (which agencies can hire) and from raw expressions of preference (which have low marginal value).

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance quantity and quality of participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Successful 'Rulemaking 2.0' civic engagement systems must involve a purposeful and continuous effort to balance 'more' and 'better' participation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design and evaluate outreach and platform features to increase participation without diluting the aggregate informational value; measurement and iterative improvement are implied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not actively facilitate participation the government does not value
rubrics_metrics.description: A democratic government should not actively facilitate public participation that it does not value
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designers and agencies should avoid promoting or amplifying forms of input that are unlikely to be useful to decisionmaking (e.g., mass submissions with no substantive content) and instead steer efforts toward productive kinds of participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overcome ignorance of the rulemaking process
rubrics_metrics.description: Ignorance of the rulemaking process — Most citizens don't know how rulemaking works
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outreach and education are necessary design components: explain how rulemaking operates and how comments are used so potential participants can contribute effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure affected parties are aware that rulemakings of interest are occurring
rubrics_metrics.description: Unawareness that rulemakings of interest are going on — Notice doesn't reach affected parties
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improve notice mechanisms and targeted outreach so that stakeholders who have relevant experiential or sectoral knowledge learn about opportunities to comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigate information overload from lengthy and complex materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Information overload from the length and complexity of rulemaking materials
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide summaries, plain-language explanations, and tools that reduce cognitive costs for potential commenters so they can find relevant portions and provide focused input.
